title: Digging Up Fresh Graves for Doctors
hook: Medical students paid grave robbers top dollar for fresh corpses.

scenes.text: In early 19th-century London, medical anatomy schools faced a severe crisis: by law, only executed murderers could be dissected.

scenes.text: With only dozens of executions a year and hundreds of eager surgery students, doctors paid fortunes to shadowy 'resurrection men'.

scenes.text: Armed with wooden spades to avoid noisy clinking on stones, grave robbers slipped into churchyards hours after a fresh burial.

scenes.voicedText: Armed with wooden spades to avoid noisy clinking on stones, grave robbers slipped into churchyards hours after a fresh burial.

scenes.text: They dug a narrow hole down to the coffin head, snapped the lid with an iron crowbar, and hauled the body up with a rope loop in fifteen minutes.

scenes.text: Terrified families installed heavy cast-iron 'mortsafes'—massive iron cages bolted over graves—and built stone watchtowers.

scenes.text: The grim trade only ended when the Anatomy Act of 1832 legalized unclaimed hospital body donations. Did you know about mortsafes?
